text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock jumped 5.2% today, capping a dramatic 19% rally over two weeks, as oil prices spiked on escalating geopolitical tension. Iran's increased tanker attacks, combined with reports of Trump administration plans for potential military operations against Iran and new Treasury sanctions on Iran's shadow fleet, sent crude prices sharply higher—Brent crude hit $125 per barrel. A refinery like Marathon benefits directly when oil prices rise, especially with U.S. refineries currently running at 92.7% capacity, meaning strong demand for refined products and healthy margins on the crude they process.

The move also reflects a tightening market backdrop: diesel prices are surging enough to draw White House policy attention, gasoline and heating oil inventories remain relatively lean, and geopolitical supply disruption risk is tangible. For a U.S. refiner, this combination of higher crude costs paired with political urgency around fuel affordability and tight product supplies creates a favorable environment for profitability, even if crude-buying pressure weighs on margins in the short term.
